Organisation(s) Affected: MTN Uganda – Mobile Money
Method / Attack Vector: Staff abused privileged access and an unreconciled suspense account while the mobile money platform had capacity problems; fictitious subscriber accounts used
Outcome / Response: Ex-employees charged in Anti-Corruption Court (embezzlement, electronic fraud); MTN tightened controls
Notes: Figures in court coverage range UGX 5–10bn; CGAP cites UGX 10bn (USD 3.4m).

Organisation(s) Affected: Uganda Revenue Authority (URA) – customs systems
Method / Attack Vector: Illegal access to customs system to push fraudulent transactions; URA did not rule out insider help
Threat Actor (as reported): 4 suspects incl. an ICT specialist and clearing agents
Outcome / Response: 4 arrested by URA enforcement and police
Notes: Losses of about UGX 2bn over roughly a year.

Organisation(s) Affected: Office of the Prime Minister, Parliament, Uganda Securities Exchange, Uganda Law Society websites; JLOS database
Method / Attack Vector: Websites defaced with spoof statements; JLOS admin passwords exposed
Notes: Protest against anti-homosexuality bill. By Dec 2012 Anonymous claimed ~9 .go.ug and ~6 commercial sites compromised (PRI).

Organisation(s) Affected: 40+ websites: ministries (Finance, ICT, Agriculture, Public Service), KCCA, NITA-U, PPDA, Uganda Police, NARO, district local governments; plus private sites
Method / Attack Vector: Mass defacement – pages replaced with group message
Notes: Private victims included Opportunity Bank, Pride Microfinance, WBS TV and hotels.

Organisation(s) Affected: Makerere University – student results
Method / Attack Vector: Alleged alteration of student grades in exchange for payment

Organisation(s) Affected: MTN Uganda – Mobile Money
Method / Attack Vector: Illegal access to mobile money system; funds wired to 7 registered agent lines

Organisation(s) Affected: Ministry of Foreign Affairs website + 20 Uganda High Commission websites
Method / Attack Vector: Mass defacement, likely via shared server
Notes: Anti-war message; date approximate – verify before citing.

Organisation(s) Affected: Makerere University – academic records system
Method / Attack Vector: Results system infiltrated to falsify marks and add ineligible graduands
Data / Systems Affected: 14,895 transcripts withheld; 58 names withdrawn from graduation list
Outcome / Response: Transcript system shut down; staff dismissed; police referral

Organisation(s) Affected: Ministry of Gender, Labour & Social Development – External Labour Information Management System
Method / Attack Vector: Intrusion to steal labour-export recruitment data; system crashed
Data / Systems Affected: Labour export company vetting records & documents

Organisation(s) Affected: Multiple banks & mobile money providers
Method / Attack Vector: 519 fraudulently swapped pre-registered SIM cards used to transfer money; duplicate national IDs used for SIM registration
Notes: Campaign-level entry, not a single incident.

Organisation(s) Affected: Pegasus Technologies (payments aggregator) – affecting MTN MoMo, Airtel Money, Stanbic Bank, Bank of Africa
Method / Attack Vector: System manipulation of bank-to-wallet transfers; ~1,630 fraudulently registered SIM cards used to cash out at agents
Threat Actor (as reported): Insider-enabled (Stanbic employee who was also Pegasus external sysadmin) + cash-out network
Outcome / Response: Bank-to-wallet services suspended; suspects arrested and charged (Dec 2020)
Primary Source(s): Eagle Online (citing CID); CEO East Africa; PML Daily
Notes: Early estimates were ~USD 3.2m; police later put loss at UGX 10.44bn.

Organisation(s) Affected: Parliament of Uganda and other government & media websites
Method / Attack Vector: Website attacks and information leaks

Organisation(s) Affected: Civil Service College Uganda website; MPs' personal data
Method / Attack Vector: Website defaced twice; MPs' personal & next-of-kin data leaked

Organisation(s) Affected: UGAFODE Microfinance Ltd
Method / Attack Vector: Unauthorised electronic theft (method not disclosed)

Organisation(s) Affected: Uganda Securities Exchange (USE) & tech partner Soft Edge
Method / Attack Vector: Unsecured server exposed investor database (~32 GB) for at least 12 days
Data / Systems Affected: Investor personal data incl. passwords & bank details
Outcome / Response: PDPO investigation found USE and Soft Edge negligent (2023)

Organisation(s) Affected: Airtel Mobile Commerce Uganda (Airtel Money)
Method / Attack Vector: Third-party betting platform used as gateway; software tweaked to auto-approve transactions; ~1,800 SIM cards used to withdraw
Outcome / Response: Airtel-to-bank services suspended; Airtel said balances unaffected
Primary Source(s): The EastAfrican; The Citizen; Pulse Uganda
Notes: Early media estimates ranged UGX 30–50bn; later reporting ~UGX 8bn.

Organisation(s) Affected: Two major commercial banks (unnamed)
Method / Attack Vector: Phishing-led intrusion; customer data accessed; USD 1m ransom demanded
Data / Systems Affected: Customer data incl. IDs, statements, credit history of high-net-worth clients
Outcome / Response: Ransom refused; banks failed over to backup data centre
Notes: Based on anonymous sources; date approximate.

Organisation(s) Affected: Bank of Uganda / Ministry of Finance Treasury
Method / Attack Vector: Two debt-service payments to IDA and AfDF diverted to private accounts in Japan and UK; insider collusion suspected
Threat Actor (as reported): 'Waste' group named in media; MoFPED officials charged
Outcome / Response: Auditor General audit; 9 MoFPED officials committed for trial; over half of funds recovered
Primary Source(s): Daily Monitor; Reuters (via CNBC Africa); The Observer
Notes: Loss = USD 6.134m + USD 8.597m per audit. Media initially reported UGX 62bn (USD 16.8m).

Organisation(s) Affected: Uganda Electricity Transmission Company Ltd (UETCL)
Method / Attack Vector: Ransomware; grid monitoring systems compromised; data theft claimed
Data / Systems Affected: Grid monitoring systems; contracts, ID documents, financial statements (claimed)
Primary Source(s): The Independent (citing INTERPOL Africa Cyberthreat Assessment 2026)
Notes: INTERPOL describes it as a suspected ransomware incident.

Organisation(s) Affected: Stanbic Bank Uganda (Standard Bank Group data incident)
Method / Attack Vector: Group-level data incident affecting a small set of Ugandan records
Data / Systems Affected: Partial data: names, emails, phone numbers, account numbers
Outcome / Response: Reported to PDPO; bank says no funds or core systems affected

Organisation(s) Affected: MTN Uganda & Stanbic Bank Uganda – service outages
Method / Attack Vector: Weekend outage of mobile money, data, ATMs, internet banking
Notes: The EastAfrican called it a cyber attack; MTN cited a data-centre power outage and neither firm attributed it to an attack.

Organisation(s) Affected: Unnamed telecom and utility company systems
Method / Attack Vector: Alleged syndicate breached telecom & utility systems causing disruptions and unauthorised deductions from customer accounts
Outcome / Response: Joint CID/immigration raids in Kampala & Wakiso; probe ongoing
Notes: May be linked to the outage above; no official loss estimate published.
